name: Vega 2
first: First chemical analysis of Venusian highland soil (Phoebe Regio, 1985); paired Halley encounter with Vega 1 fed Giotto's targeting solution
description: Twin of Vega 1, launched 6 days later (1984-12-21) for redundancy + a paired Halley armada solution. Vega 2's descent module landed 1985-06-15 in the Phoebe Regio highlands and used XRF spectrometry to find anorthosite-norite-troctolite material — the first chemical analysis of high-elevation Venusian crust. Its balloon performed identically to Vega 1's, drifting in the opposite hemisphere at ~240 km/h. The bus flew past comet 1P/Halley at 8030 km on 1986-03-09. Together the two Vega buses returned the first close-up cometary-nucleus images and refined the position fix that allowed Giotto to attempt a 596 km flyby five days later.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Proton-K / D-1 lifts Vega 2 from Baikonur 6 days behind Vega 1.

events.label: VENUS ENCOUNTER
events.note: Descent module lands at Phoebe Regio + returns first chemical analysis of highland soil.

events.label: HALLEY FLYBY
events.note: Closest approach to comet 1P/Halley at 8030 km — paired position fix for Giotto.
